question: Who originally introduced the concept of psychological defense mechanisms?
explanation: Sigmund Freud first described defense mechanisms as unconscious strategies used by the ego to manage anxiety and internal conflict. [learn more](BMP122_U2_T5#BMP122_U2_T5_h1)

question: What is the main purpose of psychological defense mechanisms in daily life?

options.D: Shielding the mind from overwhelming stress

explanation: Defense mechanisms act as mental buffers that reduce anxiety when a person faces painful or distressing emotional situations. [learn more](BMP122_U2_T5#BMP122_U2_T5_h1)

question: Where does the mind send repressed thoughts and painful memories?

options.D: Out of the body through sweat

explanation: Repression pushes distressing material out of conscious awareness and keeps it safely tucked away in the unconscious mind. [learn more](BMP122_U2_T5#BMP122_U2_T5_h2)

question: How does repression differ from simply deciding to forget something?

options.A: Conscious forgetting is permanent while repression is temporary
options.B: Repression occurs automatically without conscious awareness
options.C: Conscious forgetting requires professional therapy to reverse
options.D: Repression only happens during deep sleep cycles

explanation: A person using repression is completely unaware that their mind is hiding the distressing memory from them. [learn more](BMP122_U2_T5#BMP122_U2_T5_h2)

question: Which defense mechanism involves a deliberate, conscious choice to push a thought away?
explanation: Suppression is the intentional choice to push an unwanted thought or feeling out of awareness for the moment. [learn more](BMP122_U2_T5#BMP122_U2_T5_h3)

question: What is the main difference between repression and denial?

options.A: Denial occurs entirely in the unconscious mind unlike repression
options.B: Denial only happens to children while repression affects adults
options.C: Repression is a healthy habit while denial is always harmful
options.D: Repression hides internal memories while denial rejects external reality

explanation: Repression deals with memories and feelings already inside the mind, whereas denial refuses to accept facts happening in the outside world. [learn more](BMP122_U2_T5#BMP122_U2_T5_h3)

question: Which of the following is NOT a common sign that a patient may be struggling with repressed trauma?

options.A: Intense emotional outbursts over minor triggers
options.B: Unexplained panic or anxiety during routine procedures
options.C: Clear, detailed verbal accounts of the past event
options.D: Sudden phobias that have no obvious origin

explanation: Repressed memories are hidden from awareness, so a patient with true repression cannot give a clear verbal account of the past event. [learn more](BMP122_U2_T5#BMP122_U2_T5_h4)

question: A laboring patient shows extreme terror every time a specific nurse enters the room, yet insists she has never met this nurse before. What process likely explains her reaction?

options.A: Conscious suppression of a disagreement from earlier today
options.B: Repressed trauma triggering an unconscious fear response
options.C: Deliberate denial of the hospital admission paperwork
options.D: Rational projection of her own anger onto the midwife

explanation: Unconscious memories can drive intense emotional and physical fear responses even when the person has no conscious recollection of the trigger. [learn more](BMP122_U2_T5#BMP122_U2_T5_h4)

question: What kind of environment should a midwife create to help a deeply anxious patient feel safe?
explanation: A gentle and accepting atmosphere helps reduce anxiety and allows patients to gradually feel secure during vulnerable procedures. [learn more](BMP122_U2_T5#BMP122_U2_T5_h5)

question: Why must midwives be cautious about pushing a patient to uncover hidden emotional pain?

options.A: Unconscious memories always turn out to be completely false
options.B: Patients will immediately report the midwife to hospital management
options.C: Talking about emotions stops physical labor contractions instantly
options.D: Forced recall can overwhelm fragile coping defenses and increase distress

explanation: Defense mechanisms are there for protection, and stripping them away too quickly can cause severe psychological distress and panic. [learn more](BMP122_U2_T5#BMP122_U2_T5_h5)
